## 1. No third-party character or monster assets

Every humanoid in this game — heroes, civilians and monsters alike — is geometry built at build time by `tools/build-characters.ts` from the mesh generators in `src/characters/mesh`. No character model, rig, animation or texture was downloaded from anywhere, by anyone, at any point. Poly Haven, the only asset source this project draws on, publishes no humanoids at all.

That claim is checked mechanically every time this file is regenerated. The checks do not take the character manifest at its word — checks 4 to 6 read the download lockfile, which records what actually crossed the network — and the build fails if any of them does not hold.

| #   | Check                                                               | Result   | Evidence                                                                |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | no character entry declares a third-party provider                  | **pass** | 14 entries checked, none carries a provider field                       |
| 2   | no character entry declares a downloadable file                     | **pass** | every entry has an empty file list — nothing is fetched for a character |
| 3   | no character entry references a character-asset marketplace         | **pass** | 18 known humanoid-asset hosts checked, zero references                  |
| 4   | no character id appears in assets.lock.json                         | **pass** | 84 downloaded entries, none of them a character                         |
| 5   | assets.lock.json contains no entry of kind "character"              | **pass** | downloaded kinds: hdri x4, material x41, model x39                      |
| 6   | every downloaded file came from an allow-listed provider host       | **pass** | 376 files from dl.polyhaven.org (376)                                   |
| 7   | every CC0 map the roster reuses is a city material already credited | **pass** | 10 reused maps, each resolving to an identical entry in textures.json   |
| 8   | the manifest’s declared third-party character count is correct      | **pass** | manifest declares 0, checks 1-7 found 0                                 |
| 9   | every character names an in-repo generator                          | **pass** | all 14 generated by tools/build-characters.ts                           |

**Result: 0 third-party character assets found across 9 checks.**

The roster does reuse 10 CC0 surface maps from the city material set as fine detail on clothing and armour — weave, wear and rust. Those are ordinary Poly Haven textures, credited in section 2.1 along with every other material; check 7 confirms each one resolves to an identical entry there. They are surface detail sampled into a baked atlas, not character art: `mat.metal.corrugated`, `mat.metal.grate.rusty`, `mat.metal.panel.factory`, `mat.metal.plate.industrial`, `mat.metal.shutter.painted`, `mat.road.asphalt.clean`, `mat.roof.tiles.grey`, `mat.wall.concrete.cracked`, `mat.wall.plaster.beige`, `mat.wall.plaster.white`.

A naming convention is all that is shared: no Mixamo mesh, rig, animation or file is present in this repository, and check 3 above verifies nothing here so much as links to that domain.

## 2. Third-party assets

All 82 third-party assets come from **Poly Haven**, which releases everything it publishes under CC0-1.0 — a dedication of the work to the public domain. CC0 imposes no attribution requirement. Every author is named below regardless, because they made the thing.

| Source                               | Status              | Assets | Why                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [ambientCG](https://ambientcg.com/)  | evaluated, not used | 0      | Evaluated as a secondary CC0 source and, in the end, not drawn on: Poly Haven publishes a per-file md5 and ambientCG ships whole-material zips with no hash, so the integrity chain would have ended at the zip. |
| [Poly Haven](https://polyhaven.com/) | used                | 82     | Every asset on Poly Haven is released under CC0-1.0. Attribution is not legally required; it is recorded here anyway because the authors did the work.                                                           |

## 3. First-party assets

Generated by this repository. Nothing is downloaded and there is no upstream author to credit.

Two different licences appear below, which is worth a sentence rather than a raised eyebrow. The characters are declared `MIT`, matching [`LICENSE`](LICENSE); the two procedural materials are declared `CC0-1.0`, a full public-domain dedication. Both are this project’s own work, so both grants are ours to make, and CC0 is strictly more permissive than MIT — a recipient of the CC0 material has every right MIT would have given them and no attribution obligation on top. Nothing is in tension; the manifests simply were not written to one convention.

### 3.1 Procedural materials — 2

Poly Haven publishes no glass and no road-marking texture (verified against all 849 of its texture ids), so these two are generated instead: window glass is a shader-parameter material with no maps at all, and lane markings are an alpha decal atlas rasterised by the asset pipeline.

| Asset id            | Title                      | Origin                       | Licence                                                       |
| ------------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `mat.glass.window`  | Window Glass (procedural)  | Generated in this repository | [CC0-1.0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) |
| `mat.road.markings` | Road Markings (procedural) | Generated in this repository | [CC0-1.0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) |

### 3.2 Characters and monsters — 14

Listed in section 1 above. All original geometry, all generated in code.

### 3.3 Audio — 0 files

Every sound in this game is synthesised at runtime with the Web Audio API — punches, monsters, collapsing buildings, the crowd, the interface and the whole adaptive score are oscillators, filters and generated noise (`src/audio`). There is not one audio file in the repository, in the bundle, or fetched at runtime, so there is no audio licence to record and nothing here to re-clear. `npm run guard` enforces it: `.mp3`, `.ogg` and `.wav` are refused by the commit guard.

### 5.3 What some of those packages actually contain

A handful of the build tools are thin Node wrappers around native binaries built from another project under another licence, and one of them ships no licence text at all. The wrapper’s npm `license` field is therefore not the whole answer, so the real contents are recorded here.

| Package              | What it redistributes                                      | Upstream licence                                              | Note                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@gpu-tex-enc/basis` | Binomial LLC Basis Universal (`basisu`)                    | [Apache-2.0](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0)     | Wrapper and upstream agree on Apache-2.0.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `draco3dgltf`        | Google Draco mesh compression                              | [Apache-2.0](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0)     | Wrapper and upstream agree on Apache-2.0.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `ffmpeg-static`      | FFmpeg builds, downloaded on install                       | [GPL-3.0-or-later](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.html) | Declared in `devDependencies` but referenced by no code in this repository. It contributes nothing to any build output and nothing to the shipped game; the cleanest resolution is to drop the dependency. |
| `ktx2tools`          | Khronos KTX-Software 4.4.0 (`ktx`, `ktx2check`)            | [Apache-2.0](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0)     | The npm package declares MIT and ships no licence file; the binaries it redistributes are Khronos KTX-Software, which is Apache-2.0. Every KTX2 texture in this project is encoded by them.                |
| `playwright`         | Chromium, Firefox and WebKit builds, downloaded on install | BSD-3-Clause and others                                       | Used only to drive the verification harnesses. No browser binary is redistributed by this project — the Android APK uses the device’s own system WebView.                                                  |

Building the APK downloads the Android SDK under the [Android Software Development Kit License Agreement](https://developer.android.com/studio/terms). `scripts/android-sdk.ts` installs it into a sibling directory of this checkout, never inside it, and accepts those terms on the operator’s behalf — so anyone running that script should read them first.

## 8. One Punch Man

One Punch Man is created by ONE and illustrated by Yusuke Murata, published by Shueisha, with the anime produced by Madhouse and J.C.Staff. This is an unaffiliated, non-commercial fan project. It is not endorsed by, associated with, or approved by any of them.

No copyrighted One Punch Man material is included in this repository: no artwork, no models, no audio, no music, no fonts, no logos, no screen captures and no text from the manga or anime. Character names and the hero-ranking premise are used referentially; every asset that represents them is original geometry generated by this repository, as section 1 sets out and verifies.
